findings.text: Init time test driver runs paired success and failure checks for all width specific unsigned and signed converters and for unsigned and signed scaled decimal 64 converters, then returns a negative invalid argument status so the test code does not remain loaded.

For the unsigned scaled decimal helper, success and failure tables assert rejection of empty input, lone newline, lone dot, lone plus, alphabetic and trailing junk, leading or trailing blanks, any minus sign and out of range magnitudes, with acceptance limited to well formed non negative decimal text that fits after scaling.

For the signed scaled decimal helper, tables assert acceptance of optional leading plus or minus, integer only text scaled by trailing zeros, fraction only text with leading dot, short fraction padding, truncation of excess fraction digits, a single trailing newline and boundary magnitudes at the signed extremes, with rejection of empty, sign only, dot only, junk and overflow cases.

Both scaled decimal suites assert that scales at and above twenty succeed only for zero and for extremely small fractional magnitudes that still fit the 64 bit result, while ordinary magnitudes such as a tenth or unity fail at those scales.
First expected bitmap length in bits is defined as the byte size of the first expected word table multiplied by eight, used as the sweep bound for the ordered set bit checks.

Parselist test case is a read only record holding an expected error integer, an input text pointer, a pointer to expected words, a bit count and a flags word, iterated as a table by the list and hex parse checks.
Harness defines a timing flag with value one, a no length flag with value two, and a second expected length in bits derived from the byte size of the second expected table times eight.

Equality helpers compare single integers, compare bitmaps over a bit count, render a bitmap to list form in a shared page sized buffer before string comparison, compare bounded strings and validate eight bit clump extraction with range and nonzero guards, each reporting file and line on mismatch and returning a boolean tallied into total and failed counts by wrapper macros.

Zero clear fill set and copy checks assert prefix and cross word behavior on a thousand bit map, including clearing or zeroing a prefix length, filling a prefix length, full range fill, copying exact bit counts and word tail handling where short copies leave later words beyond the covered words unchanged except for padding effects, all verified via list rendering.

Ordered set bit checks assert correct nth set position over a sparse map plus out of range queries returning end of range and a full sweep over the first expected table, while zero area checks assert start search honoring start offset, required length, alignment mask and offset constraint over a patterned map with scattered holes.

Region checks assert discovery of increasing power of two free blocks and release returning weight to zero, replace checks assert masked choice between two sources under a mask in both source orders from both cleared and filled destinations, and scatter gather checks assert compaction and expansion through a sparse mask with round trip stability.

List parse table asserts singletons, hyphen ranges, stride selections of used counts over group sizes, comma groups with blanks and empty groups ignored, empty input meaning empty set, case insensitive all meaning full set, symbolic last bit marker, and distinct malformed, reversed range, out of range and overflow failures.

Hex parse table asserts comma separated groups of hexadecimal words in high to low order with surrounding and inner blanks and empty groups tolerated, empty and zero meaning zero, exact fit versus overflow at stated bit lengths, unbounded input length when the no length flag is set, and distinct malformed and overflow failures.

Print check allocates page sized bitmap and text buffers, fills the bitmap with ones, formats the full range through the list formatter, asserts returned length and textual span match expectation and logs elapsed time, skipping silently when allocation fails and freeing both buffers on exit.

List comparison rewrites one static init data scratch buffer on every call so each result is valid only until the next comparison and concurrent callers would interleave, and several scratch and expected tables reside in init only storage usable solely during init.
